notes: The enterprise hooks.json applies to every user on the machine. Cursor runs hooks fail-open: a crash or timeout lets the call through unless failClosed is set, which selfhost leaves off. If selfhost agents configure also wrote ~/.cursor/hooks.json, Cursor runs both.
Team rules, team hooks and the MCP allowlist live in the Cursor dashboard (Teams and Enterprise) with no API. Not checked against a Cursor Teams account.
Cursor's MCP tool names (MCP:<tool>) carry no server, so rules naming mcp__<server>__<tool> never match in Cursor.

rules.detail: Cursor has no admin-managed deny list for commands: the team dashboard sets run modes and has no API, and cli-config.json permissions are per user and CLI only. The selfhost hook checks it.

~/.cursor/permissions.json sits in each user's home, so it holds only where device management delivers and locks it, and a dashboard MCP allowlist replaces it. The selfhost hook checks the rest.
